title: Two things set side by side (By contrast / Conversely)
subtitle: Transitions · 27 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **27 of the official questions in Transitions are this one** — 9 Easy, 11 Medium, 7 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You see two parallel categories, groups or cases described with the same sentence frame, where one attribute flips: above/below, one/many, follows the rule/breaks the rule.
- Often the blank sits mid-sentence after the second subject, set off by commas.
- The choices mix one contrast word with example, sequence and conclusion words.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Name the subject of each sentence and the attribute given for each.
- 2) If the subjects differ and the attributes are opposites, pick the comparison-contrast word (by contrast, conversely, in comparison only if it's framed as a difference).
- 3) Rule out 'similarly' and 'likewise', which need the same attribute.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: In the harder versions, sentence one states a general tendency and the blank sentence brings in one specific case.
You reach for 'for example' because a specific item follows.
But that case goes against the tendency, so it's a contrast, not an illustration.
Before you call something an example, check that the specific case actually agrees with the general claim.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
